source_text.docs/issues/ISS-0816.yaml: CORRECTED 2026-09-24 by ISSUE-FIXER (WF03-ISS0816-20260925 Step 1). This record originally claimed: "has_more IS genuinely emitted by lib/letflow/audit.ex (:276, :295-297), so the field is real for the audit route and absent everywhere Pagination.Page is used. One type covering both cannot be correct for either." **That is false, and it was the record's central premise.** audit.ex:276/295-297 is the INTERNAL return of Letflow.Audit.list_entries/1. lib/letflow/routers/audit.ex:203-204 consumes it, passes has_more to the private next_cursor/2, and then page_body/2 (:308-320) hand-builds %{"items", "next_cursor", "count"} as an explicit INV-2 allowlist. has_more never crosses the HTTP boundary. So NO route in Letflow emits has_more. CursorPage<T>.has_more covers zero wire shapes, not two.

task.description: WF-03 Step 2 (fix design) for ISS-0816, on branch feature/WF03-ISS0816-20260925. Produce lib/letflow/design/iss-0816-cursorpage-has-more-audit.md. Start from the refuted premise: ISS-0816 originally claimed lib/letflow/audit.ex emits has_more so one shared type covered two wire shapes; it does not. audit.ex:276/295-297 is the internal return of Letflow.Audit.list_entries/1, lib/letflow/routers/audit.ex:203-204 passes that has_more to a private next_cursor/2, and page_body/2 (:308-320) hand-builds an INV-2 allowlist of exactly {"items", "next_cursor", "count"}. No route in Letflow emits has_more, so CursorPage<T>.has_more covers zero wire shapes. ISSUE-FIXER has already tabulated all 15 CursorPage<T> call sites and derived the route table by runtime introspection of __authz_routes__/0; carry that table into the design and verify it by spot-check rather than redoing it. Adopt ISSUE-FIXER's recommended shape unless it can be shown wrong: delete has_more from the shared type, then split on the axis the backend actually varies on -- CursorPage<T> = {items, next_cursor} for the 7 two-key sites, and a new CountedCursorPage<T> = {items, next_cursor, count} for the rest. Four decisions must be stated and justified rather than surveyed: (a) whether the two client-side fabrication sites audit.ts:71 and promotions.ts:265, which compute has_more: Boolean(response.next_cursor) and have zero consumers, are deleted or kept under an honest name; (b) whether GroupMemberPage, RawAuditPage and ISS-0711's TenantListResponse collapse into CountedCursorPage<T> in this run or are left alone, given that collapsing is tidier but widens blast radius and GroupMemberPage was created only the day before by ISS-0765 (dec06da7); (c) whether AC3's GroupsPage members dialog should follow next_cursor or state the truncation in the UI, noting the real default page size is 50 (pagination.ex:51 @default_page_size via identity.ex:546-548) and that .members is now GroupMemberPage rather than CursorPage<T>, so AC3 is no longer coupled to the type change -- including whether it should stay in this run's scope at all; and (d) what TYPE rows 7 and 8 of the audit table (modulesApi.list, modulesApi.listShares) should carry, given they target /api/v1/admin/modules and /admin/module-shares, which do not exist -- Letflow.Routers.ProcessModules is listed at router.ex:82 as deferred to S5 and is filed separately as ISS-0822, so only the type question is in scope. Deliver exact type shapes, exact per-site before/after at file:line, and a test matrix. Design only: no implementation code, no function bodies. Out of scope and already filed, do not design fixes for: the dead limit/offset on definitionsApi.search (ISS-0820); the four test fixtures hand-writing has_more (ISS-0821); the nonexistent modules router (ISS-0822); ISS-0811, ISS-0812, ISS-0813, ISS-0814, ISS-0815. Trap flagged by ISSUE-FIXER: TimelineFeed.tsx's hasMore prop is camelCase, derived from next_cursor, and entirely unrelated -- do not touch it. Timestamps must come from date -u, not the session date. Commit and push the design and this handoff to origin/feature/WF03-ISS0816-20260925, and run mix letflow.lint_handoffs --dir on this file before finishing. REWORK ITERATION 1 (from step-02b-design-gate.json, commit 2da52436): CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR returned FAIL on two blockers, both in the T7 guard specification. BLOCKER-1, section 4 contradicts section 7 row T7: section 4 requires the CursorPage<T> docblock to state that no route emits has_more, while T7 as written bans that bare token across web/src with only two exemptions, neither of which is api.ts, so FRONTEND-DEV following both sections literally would fail npm run guards. BLOCKER-2, T7's exemption list is incomplete and this was measured: web/src/api/__tests__/identity.groupsApi.test.ts:63 carries a truthful prose comment naming has_more, is inside source-scan.spec.ts's glob which has no __tests__ exclusion, is never edited by section 5, and is not exempted -- the validator's worktree produced exactly two source-scan violations, at web/src/types/api.ts:14 and that file. Section 8 item 8's claim that the guard is satisfiable with zero exemptions outside __tests__ is therefore measurably false, its cause being a grep -v __tests__ filter applied to evidence for a guard whose appliesTo is 'source'. The recommended single fix, which closes both at once, is to narrow T7's regex from the bare token to the code form of the field -- an object-literal key or a property access -- so prose naming the field is unaffected while the guard keeps its real purpose; adopt that or justify something better, and make sections 4, 7 T7 and 8 item 8 end up consistent with each other. Also fix, non-blocking: rest decision (c)'s justification on INV-D rather than on write corruption, since GroupMemberAddResult.created (api.ts:498-502) makes the backend add idempotent and the conclusion is unaffected; @default_page_size is at pagination.ex:51 not :53; specify the truncated edge case at exactly 20 pages; and section 10's (unfiled) row is now ISS-0823 (queue task 823, GH #1814, filed mid-gate in ea1a43a4). result.summary: Revision 2 of lib/letflow/design/iss-0816-cursorpage-has-more-audit.md. Both blockers are closed by one change, and the whole of the gate's what_must_change list (items 1-8) is addressed. BLOCKER-1 and BLOCKER-2 were the same mistake -- T7 banned a WORD when the invariant INV-A is about a FIELD -- so T7's regex is narrowed from the bare token to the three code forms the field can actually take in TypeScript: a property access, an object-literal or type-member key, and a string-literal key. Final regex /\.has_more\b|\bhas_more\s*\??\s*:|["']has_more["']/. Prose is unaffected because a comment names the field inside backticks and a closing backtick is neither whitespace nor a colon, so section 4's required docblock is legal and identity.groupsApi.test.ts:63's truthful comment needs no exemption. The final allowedPaths set is therefore unchanged from revision 1 -- exactly the two ISS-0821 fixtures, PromotionReviewListPage.test.tsx and TaskInboxPage.test.tsx, both of which still write the code form has_more: false -- and the inline comment still says those exemptions go when ISS-0821 lands. The cost of narrowing is stated rather than hidden: a bare has_more in prose outside backticks and not followed by a colon is no longer caught, which is accepted because prose cannot make a request or type a response. Section 4 now also carries the authoring rule that keeps the two consistent: in prose, write the token inside backticks and never immediately followed by a colon. Section 8 item 8 is struck through rather than deleted, with the cause named -- the grep -v __tests__ filter was applied to evidence for a guard whose appliesTo is 'source', while section 5.6 had already reasoned correctly that src/**/__tests__ is inside tsc's scope and simply did not carry that across. The unfiltered grep returns fourteen occurrences across eight files, and the validator's two measured violations are quoted. Everything is re-measured, not asserted. The narrowed regex was first checked against 20 hand-built strings, 10 must-match and 10 must-not, all correct; then the full probe was re-applied in the working tree with section 4's real docblock prose, section 5's full edit set, the new PATTERNS entry and T8's two fixtures, and reverted afterwards with git checkout plus git clean, tree confirmed clean. Results: npm run guards 4 files / 52 tests all passed, up from 48 because of T8's four fixture assertions, with source-scan reporting ZERO violations while api.ts carries the required has_more prose and identity.groupsApi.test.ts:63 is untouched and unexempted; tsc -b --force exit 0; npm run test 125 files / 890 tests passed. The four non-blocking corrections are applied: decision (c) now rests on INV-D and explicitly withdraws the 'wrong write path' framing, noting GroupMemberAddResult.created at api.ts:498-502 makes the backend add idempotent, with the conclusion unchanged because it never depended on corruption -- the dropdown is a DIFFERENT control from the member list and is derived from the truncated set, which is what a notice on the list cannot repair; pagination.ex:51; section 6.1 now specifies truncated as reporting whether members were left unfetched rather than whether the cap was reached, so a group of exactly 4000 returns truncated false and only a non-null next_cursor on the 20th response returns true; and section 10 names ISS-0823. One new consequence was found while re-reading identity.groupsApi.test.ts for BLOCKER-2 and is now section 6.3 and test T9: adding listAllMembers makes groupsApi's surface seven functions, which breaks T-0765-SURFACE at :229 (an exact-equality assertion over Object.keys) and needs a new row in T-0765-NO-ADMIN-PREFIX's hand-maintained surfaceRows at :251-258. Both are ISS-0765's guards working as designed, not defects, and are named so FRONTEND-DEV does not meet them as a surprise. Sections 1-5 and the route-to-shape mapping are carried forward unchanged, as the gate directed.

result.how_the_section_4_t7_contradiction_was_r: By narrowing the guard to the field, not the word. T7 exists to serve INV-A, which is about a field being declared or accessed -- not about the nine characters appearing anywhere in the tree. Revision 1 conflated the two, which is what made section 4's required docblock illegal and what made identity.groupsApi.test.ts:63 a false positive. The narrowed regex matches only the three ways TypeScript can express the field: a property access (\.has_more\b), an object-literal or type-member key (\bhas_more\s*\??\s*: -- which also covers the optional form has_more?: boolean), and a string-literal key (["']has_more["']). Prose is structurally safe because comments name the field inside backticks, and a closing backtick is neither whitespace nor a colon. The alternatives the gate listed were both rejected and the trade-offs are recorded in the design: exempting web/src/types/api.ts would gut the guard at the single most important file it protects, and rewording section 4 to avoid the literal token would cost section 4 its stated purpose, which is to name the field explicitly so nobody re-files ISS-0816 for a sixth time. The accepted cost of narrowing -- a bare has_more in prose outside backticks and not followed by a colon is no longer caught -- is stated in section 7.1 rather than left for a reader to discover.
